name: Inductive Miner
description: Leemans' Inductive Miner (IM and IMf) in Rust: recursively cuts the directly-follows graph into a block-structured process tree. Unlike Alpha or Heuristics Miner it always returns a sound model, and IMf tolerates infrequent behavior without giving that up.

variant.title: Variant
variant.description: IM guarantees the model can replay every trace in the log. IMf gives that up in exchange for ignoring infrequent behavior, and is the usual choice on a real log.

noiseThreshold.title: Noise threshold
noiseThreshold.description: IMf only. How weak a path has to be, relative to the strongest alternative leaving the same activity, before it is treated as noise. At 0 nothing is filtered and IMf equals IM; at 1 only the strongest path out of each activity survives. Filtering is a fallback — it is applied only where the unfiltered log yields no cut. Re-running is not instant, so this is not a live slider.

maxActivities.title: Distinct activities
maxActivities.description: This is not an event limit. Every event is read, however many there are — a 561,000-event log takes well under a second, because events are collapsed into repeated trace patterns before the algorithm runs. What this caps is the number of distinct activity labels, keeping the most frequent. It is a safety ceiling for pathological logs rather than a modeling choice: dropping an activity can remove a whole branch, and a run that hits the ceiling reports how many it lost. A large real log has a few hundred distinct activities. Cost grows with distinct activities, and with how little structure the log has — not with the number of events.

recommends.reason: draws the process trees this plugin produces

citation.text: Leemans, S.J.J., Fahland, D., van der Aalst, W.M.P. (2013). Discovering Block-Structured Process Models from Event Logs — A Constructive Approach. Petri Nets 2013, LNCS 7927, 311–329. Infrequent-behavior variant: Leemans, Fahland, van der Aalst (2014), BPM Workshops 2013, LNBIP 171, 66–78.
